# osm-pmtiles

**Vector-tile maps of your OpenStreetMap regions, for the offline browser map**

- **Version recorded:** station
- **Categories:** `navigation-maps`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/systemed/tilemaker>
- **Needs first:** `osm-regions`, `vector-map-kit`, `tilemaker`, `gdal-bin`

## What it does

Builds one PMTiles file of vector tiles per region `osm-regions` downloaded, with the archive's tilemaker and tilemaker's own OpenMapTiles profile, as the operator in a staging directory. The files land under /usr/local/share/hammunition/data/osm-pmtiles/, and `hammunition reference serve` shows them as a map in a browser at http://127.0.0.1:8480/map/, drawn with the OSM Bright style, with your position from `hammunition maps gps-tether`. Since D-075 the profile adds one `infra` layer at street zoom (power lines and plants, masts, pipelines, water works, hydrants: about 2.5 % more on Delaware), drawn with power coloured by voltage after Open Infrastructure Map; a region built before it is rebuilt once at the next install.

## Why you would want it

A map anyone can open in a browser, with no program to learn, and no network: streets, labels, water, parks and buildings to zoom 14 of every region you chose, drawn on this machine. It is the offline stand-in for an online web map, and a tile source the rest of the station can read later. Navit and QMapShack stay the navigators; this is the map to glance at.

## Before it will work

`osm-regions` with at least one region set in station config, `vector-map-kit`, and the archive's `tilemaker` 3.0 or newer and `gdal-bin`; all install first. With no regions set this unit is deferred by name. Ubuntu 24.04 and the releases built on it carry tilemaker 2.4, which cannot write PMTiles; the plan defers this unit there by name.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`navigation`](../profiles/navigation.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install osm-pmtiles --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

The tiles are built on this machine from the regions you installed and served with no network by `hammunition reference serve` at http://127.0.0.1:8480/map/ , on this machine only. The page loads nothing from anywhere else. Your position appears on it only while the GPS tether runs. Not yet looked at on the field laptop's own browser for the infrastructure layer.

## First useful task

Run `hammunition reference serve` and open http://127.0.0.1:8480/map/ ; your installed regions are drawn, and layers written by `hammunition maps infra` are listed beside the map with a show/hide box.

## How it installs

- converted from osm-regions by tilemaker-pmtiles (ODbL-1.0, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright)

## Known problems

Measured by the spike on one region, Delaware (22 MB download), on 2026-09-29, with osmdata's simplified water polygons as the ocean: 10 to 37 s, 0.49 GB of memory with tilemaker's --store (which the engine passes) against 2.8 GB without it, and a PMTiles file 0.91 times the download, zooms 0 to 14. The engine's own run, with Natural Earth's ocean, has not been run with a real tilemaker yet (none was installed on the development host); the scratch that --store writes was not measured, so the plan allows three times the download. Coasts at street zoom follow Natural Earth's 1:10m line. tilemaker writes one output per run, so no .mbtiles is made: AIS-catcher reads .mbtiles itself and is not served by this. The file carries the Open Database License obligations of the data, and the page draws the credit the OpenMapTiles schema's CC-BY licence requires.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- Follows osm-regions: a region whose downloaded file changed is built again on the next install, and one that did not is skipped.

## Where to get help with the software itself

tilemaker's GitHub issues (https://github.com/systemed/tilemaker/issues) for the conversion; problems in the map data are fixed in OpenStreetMap (https://www.openstreetmap.org/fixthemap).
